text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Risk modelling teams at banks are female-dominated in some institutions and all-female panels occur by chance; raising it signals grievance rather than substance and tends to make employers defensive and legalistic. It also weakens your credible complaint.

Your stronger ground is procedural: you've waited two weeks for written reasons. Chase that in writing, politely, with a deadline, citing the job description's stated criteria and asking how each shortlisted candidate was scored against them.

Note too that "head of" roles often weight regulatory fluency, stakeholder management and supervisory dialogue above technical depth — a master's plus regulatory breadth can legitimately beat a PhD. Judge the decision once you see the scoring.
